q: What must be done to burred pipe ends before joining?
o: Leave them, since the joint seals them
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Burrs inside the pipe catch paper and solids and start blockages.

q: For an underground cleanout, what horizontal clearance from a wall is required?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Clearance in front of cleanouts: 305 mm for pipes 51 mm and smaller, 450 mm for larger pipes; underground, 450 mm vertically and 750 mm horizontally.

q: Which bend makes a 60° change of direction in drainage?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Drainage bends: 1/16 bend = 22.5°, 1/8 bend = 45°, 1/6 bend = 60°.

q: Which fixtures are counted as suds-producing?
o: Tubs, washers, kitchen sinks and dishwashers
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Suds from these fixtures pile up at the base of stacks and can blow out traps.

q: When must an extra cleanout be added on a drainage line with several bends?
o: When the total change of direction exceeds 135°
Never; one cleanout per line is enough
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Rods cannot pass many bends. More than 135° of total offset calls for another cleanout.

q: What is the maximum trap loading for a 76 mm trap?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Maximum trap loading: 32 mm 1 FU, 38 mm 3 FU, 51 mm 4 FU, 76 mm 6 FU, 102 mm 8 FU.

q: How must plumbing fixtures drain into the sewage disposal system?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Gravity drainage has no moving parts to fail. Pumps are used only for fixtures below the sewer.

q: What cleanout size is used on a 38 mm drainage pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Cleanout sizes: 38 and 51 mm pipe take a 38 mm cleanout (11.5 threads per 25.4 mm); 64 and 76 mm pipe take 64 mm (8 threads); 102 mm pipe takes 89 mm (8 threads).

q: What rule applies to drainage fittings and the pipe they join?
o: Always one size larger than the pipe
Always one size smaller than the pipe
Any material, as long as it is threaded
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Mismatched sizes form ledges that catch solids.

q: What clearance is required in front of a cleanout on pipe larger than 51 mm?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Clearance in front of cleanouts: 305 mm for pipes 51 mm and smaller, 450 mm for larger pipes; underground, 450 mm vertically and 750 mm horizontally.

q: Which bend makes a 22.5° change of direction in drainage?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Drainage bends: 1/16 bend = 22.5°, 1/8 bend = 45°, 1/6 bend = 60°.

q: How is a sewage sump vented?
o: Into the room where it is located
Into the building's other vents only
With a vent that extends through the roof
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: The vent lets air in and out as the sump fills and empties. It must not join air vents from the ejector.

q: When may a cleanout be omitted at the upper end of a horizontal drain?
o: When it is under 1.5 m and serves no sink or urinal
When the drain is under 15 m long
When the drain serves a water closet
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Sinks and urinals clog often, so even short drains serving them need cleanouts.

q: What is the maximum trap loading for a 38 mm trap?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Maximum trap loading: 32 mm 1 FU, 38 mm 3 FU, 51 mm 4 FU, 76 mm 6 FU, 102 mm 8 FU.

q: What is the standard slope of horizontal drainage pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Pipes 102 mm and larger may drop to 1% where 2% is impractical.

q: How does a vertical drain turn to horizontal?
o: Through a sanitary tee on its back
Through a 45° wye, long sweep or offset
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: A gentle change keeps the falling water from slamming into the horizontal pipe.

q: May galvanized steel or wrought iron drainage pipe be laid underground?
o: No; keep it 152 mm above ground
Yes, if the soil is dry
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Galvanizing corrodes fast in soil.

q: Where must a cleanout with a cover plate be?
o: Above grade, where it can be reached
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Cleanouts are useless if they cannot be reached.

q: For drainage sizing, how many fixture units are assigned to a continuous flow of about 0.063 L/s (1 gpm)?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Continuous flows such as pumps and cooling equipment are turned into fixture units at 2 FU per 0.063 L/s.

q: What valves are required on a sewage pump discharge line?
o: A check valve and a gate valve
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: The check valve stops the rising main draining back; the gate valve isolates it for repair.

q: What cleanout size is used on a 76 mm drainage pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Cleanout sizes: 38 and 51 mm pipe take a 38 mm cleanout (11.5 threads per 25.4 mm); 64 and 76 mm pipe take 64 mm (8 threads); 102 mm pipe takes 89 mm (8 threads).

q: Why are drainage fitting threads tapped at an angle?
o: So the pipe stays perfectly level
So the pipe falls at 2% (20 mm per m)
So the joint needs no compound
So the pipe can be vented without a fitting
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: A straight pipe screwed into the fitting then slopes at the standard grade.

q: How far may an underfloor cleanout be from an access opening?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: A person must be able to crawl to it with rods and tools.

q: How does a horizontal drain turn to vertical?
o: Through a short 90° elbow on its back
Through a 45° or 60° wye, or a sanitary tee
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Horizontal-to-vertical is the one direction where sanitary tees are allowed, since the water falls away from the inlet.

q: Where are suds-relief rules not applied?
o: Houses and stacks of up to three storeys
Hotels and hospitals of any height
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Suds only build up enough to cause trouble in taller stacks.

q: Which way must a cleanout open?
o: With the flow, or at a right angle to it
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: The rod has to go downstream, the way the blockage will move.

q: What is the maximum trap loading for a 102 mm trap?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Maximum trap loading: 32 mm 1 FU, 38 mm 3 FU, 51 mm 4 FU, 76 mm 6 FU, 102 mm 8 FU.

q: How is drainage below the crown of the public sewer handled?
o: It is connected to the sewer by gravity anyway
It discharges into a seepage pit
It discharges into an approved watertight sump and is pumped up
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Water cannot flow uphill, and gravity would let the sewer back up into the building.

q: What cleanout size is used on a 51 mm drainage pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Cleanout sizes: 38 and 51 mm pipe take a 38 mm cleanout (11.5 threads per 25.4 mm); 64 and 76 mm pipe take 64 mm (8 threads); 102 mm pipe takes 89 mm (8 threads).

q: What kind of fittings are used on screwed (threaded) drainage pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Recessed fittings leave a smooth, flush bore with no ledge at the joint.

q: For an underground cleanout, what vertical clearance is required?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Clearance in front of cleanouts: 305 mm for pipes 51 mm and smaller, 450 mm for larger pipes; underground, 450 mm vertically and 750 mm horizontally.

q: Which bend makes a 45° change of direction in drainage?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Drainage bends: 1/16 bend = 22.5°, 1/8 bend = 45°, 1/6 bend = 60°.

q: How close to a vertical-to-horizontal change of direction may a fixture connect in a suds zone?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Suds pile up where a stack turns horizontal and can push out through nearby traps.

q: Where may a two-way cleanout be installed?
o: On a vent stack above the roof
Between the building drain and sewer
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: One two-way fitting lets rods go either up into the building or out to the sewer.

q: What is the maximum trap loading for a 51 mm trap?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Maximum trap loading: 32 mm 1 FU, 38 mm 3 FU, 51 mm 4 FU, 76 mm 6 FU, 102 mm 8 FU.

q: Where 2% is impractical, what minimum slope may a drain 102 mm or larger have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Bigger pipes carry solids at lower slopes.

q: What is the maximum spacing of cleanouts on a horizontal drain?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Standard rods reach about 15 m.

q: Where may vitrified clay drainage pipe NOT be used?
o: Above ground, or on pumped lines
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Clay is brittle and cannot take internal pressure or impact above ground.

q: What clearance is required in front of a cleanout on pipe 51 mm and smaller?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Clearance in front of cleanouts: 305 mm for pipes 51 mm and smaller, 450 mm for larger pipes; underground, 450 mm vertically and 750 mm horizontally.

q: When may two fixtures set side by side or back to back share one vertical drain?
o: Only if both are water closets
When both traps are within vent distance
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: A shared drain works if each trap still has its vent within the allowed distance.

q: How is a sewage sump covered?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: The cover keeps sewer gas in and people out.

q: What cleanout size is used on a 102 mm drainage pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Cleanout sizes: 38 and 51 mm pipe take a 38 mm cleanout (11.5 threads per 25.4 mm); 64 and 76 mm pipe take 64 mm (8 threads); 102 mm pipe takes 89 mm (8 threads).

q: What is the maximum trap loading for a 32 mm trap?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Maximum trap loading: 32 mm 1 FU, 38 mm 3 FU, 51 mm 4 FU, 76 mm 6 FU, 102 mm 8 FU.

q: Are cleanouts required on pressure (pumped) drainage lines?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Pumped lines can block too, and must be cleanable.

q: How does one horizontal drain join another horizontal drain?
o: Through a 45° wye or wye and 1/8 bend
Through a sanitary tee on its back
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Sanitary tees on the flat send flow against the other branch and cause backups.

q: Which of these is NOT a listed drainage pipe material?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Listed materials include cast and ductile iron, galvanized steel, lead, copper, brass, PVC-DWV and extra-strength clay.

q: Where is the cleanout for an interceptor placed?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: A cleanout inside would sit in the grease and be unreachable.

q: What is drainage piping sized from?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Each fixture has a fixture-unit value. The code table gives the pipe size for the total.

q: What is the minimum discharge pipe from a sump that receives a water closet?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: The pump must pass solids from the water closet.

q: What cleanout size is used on a 64 mm drainage pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 7
n: Cleanout sizes: 38 and 51 mm pipe take a 38 mm cleanout (11.5 threads per 25.4 mm); 64 and 76 mm pipe take 64 mm (8 threads); 102 mm pipe takes 89 mm (8 threads).
